about: Signed transactions: wire_base64 is the full serialized transaction, message_base64 the bytes every signer signed. account_keys are the message's static keys with the privileges its header gives them; instructions are the compiled instructions, indexing account_keys (then a v0 message's looked-up addresses, writable before readonly). built_instructions are the builder's instructions, whose per-instruction signer and writable flags the wire does not carry. program is what the escrow program and runtime did with it on LiteSVM: ok, the Anchor error name it refused with, or the runtime's TransactionError when no Anchor error was logged. It is not a payer-side verdict: a shape the program accepts may still be one a payer must refuse to sign.

context.keys_about: every key's secret is 32 bytes of its seed (Keypair::new_from_array([seed; 32])), so a test can re-sign as it

encoding: u64 and i64 are decimal strings, smaller integers JSON numbers; keys and signatures are base58; account data, instruction data, transactions and events are base64; every other byte field is hex. The exception is receipt_value, a copy of proto's receipt_v3.value shape: its integers are JSON numbers and its ticket_id and deployment base64
